claim: A viral quote was posted by Khairallah AL-Awady in late May 2026: 'You're not supposed to prompt Claude. You're supposed to build a system that prompts itself.'
source_quote: In late May 2026, a quote attributed to an Anthropic engineer started circulating across X and LinkedIn: "You're not supposed to prompt Claude. You're supposed to build a system that prompts itself." Khairallah AL-Awady, an engineer with a large following on X, posted it alongside a breakdown of what he called "one of the best workflows I've seen in a long time."

claim: CLAUDE.md files contain coding standards, architecture decisions, preferred libraries, and user preferences
source_quote: It reads your CLAUDE.md file — a project-level configuration that tells the agent your coding standards, your architecture decisions, your preferred libraries, what to avoid, and how you want things done.

claim: Claude Code automatically loads git branch, last five commits, and working tree status into context
source_quote: It pulls your current git branch, your last five commits, and your working tree status.

claim: Prompt engineering is about writing instructions while context engineering is about designing the entire information environment
source_quote: prompt engineering is about writing instructions. Context engineering is about designing the entire information environment the agent operates in.

source_quote: Anthropic's agent loop documentation describes this explicitly: "LLMs autonomously using tools in a loop."

source_quote: A Reddit user documented running Claude Code for 9 hours and 27 minutes straight, chaining four self-paced goal commands, producing 45 commits and 14,259 lines of code autonomously.

claim: During autonomous operation, 45 commits and 14,259 lines of code were produced

claim: Security researcher Chaofan Shou discovered a 59.8-megabyte source map file in March 2026
source_quote: In March 2026, security researcher Chaofan Shou discovered a 59.8-megabyte source map file accidentally bundled inside the `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` npm package.

claim: The leak exposed 512,000 lines of Claude Code's source code
source_quote: It exposed 512,000 lines of Claude Code's source code.

claim: KAIROS was referenced over 150 times in the leaked codebase
source_quote: Buried in that codebase, referenced over 150 times, was something called KAIROS — named after the Greek concept of "the right moment."

claim: KAIROS is named after the Greek concept of 'the right moment'
source_quote: KAIROS — named after the Greek concept of "the right moment."

claim: The Buddy system has 18 species and 5 rarity tiers
source_quote: The leak also revealed a Buddy system — a Tamagotchi-style terminal pet with 18 species and 5 rarity tiers.

claim: Anthropic acknowledges that 'overly aggressive compaction can result in the loss of subtle but critical context'
source_quote: Anthropic's own blog acknowledges the risk: "overly aggressive compaction can result in the loss of subtle but critical context whose importance only becomes apparent later."

claim: Anthropic's Zero Trust for AI Agents ebook was published May 2026
source_quote: Anthropic's own Zero Trust for AI Agents ebook, published May 2026, proposes a "bounded trust" framework for exactly this scenario.

source_quote: In episode 99, we covered why your AI agent dies the second you close the terminal — the statelessness problem.

source_quote: In episode 100, we covered Opus 4.8's dynamic workflows that orchestrate up to 1,000 subagents in a single run.
